# E018 -- A Punt

## Metadata
- **Brand:** A Punt (full name: A Punt Media)
- **Industry:** Media / Broadcasting (public broadcaster of Valencia)
- **Year:** 2017 (October)
- **Region:** CA/ES (Comunitat Valenciana, Spain)
- **Language:** Catalan/Valencian
- **Source file:** a-punt-pdf.pdf
- **Pages sampled:** 1-2, 6-7, 12-13, 18-35

## Brand Strategy
- Brand essence rooted in Valencian culture and identity -- the circular "punt" (dot) represents a meeting point ("punt de trobada"), referencing how Valencians gather around circular objects (tables, paella pans, plazas).
- Tagline: "L'espai public de comunicacio valencia" (The Valencian public communication space).
- The lowercase "a" is deliberately chosen to convey serenity, dialogue, youth, creativity, and entertainment.
- Brand architecture includes sub-brands for TV, radio, digital, and a children's channel ("A Punt La Colla").

## Logo
- Primary mark: a geometric lowercase "a" inside a circle (the "punt"/dot).
- The circle also functions as an isolation device for on-screen watermark ("mosca") usage across multiple media.
- Multiple versions: Version 1 (primary), Version 1 negative (for dark backgrounds), Version 1.1 (full name with descriptor), Version 2 (alternative).
- Strict misuse rules; logo must remain in black or white only for corporate use.
- Minimum size: 5 mm (print), 20 px (digital).
- Clear space ("area de respecte") defined around the mark.

## Typography
- **Primary typeface:** Gotham (Bold and Book weights) by Hoefler & Co.
- Chosen for its geometric nature, matching the round "a" of the logo -- described as clean, current, rotund, with character.
- Fallback: Arial.
- Specific rule for Valencian accented characters: 1/3 x-height spacing above capitals for accent marks.
- Two tonal modes: all-caps Gotham Bold for formal/serious messaging; mixed-case Gotham Book for fresh/playful communication.

## Color
- **Corporate (primary):** Black and White -- representing journalistic rigour, transparency, and public character.
- **Blue family:** Turquoise (#008CD6, Pantone 2925 C) and Cobalt (#003099, Pantone 7687 C) -- representing the Mediterranean sea and Valencian ceramics.
- **Orange/Yellow family:** Orange (#F7932C, Pantone 144) and Terracotta Red (#CF4520, Pantone 173 C) -- representing the land, oranges, sun, and warmth.
- Maximum 3 colours on screen at any time (plus black/white).
- Exception: children's channel "La Colla" may use full palette freely.
- Yellow does not allow white text overlaid.

## Graphics / Illustration
- Geometric graphic language derived from the circular motif of the logo.
- Sub-brand construction system: each sub-brand uses a variant inside or alongside the circle container.
- "Elements de connexio" (connection elements) used for signage and linking brand elements across applications.

## Photography
- Not explicitly detailed in sampled pages; photography appears subordinate to colour and graphic system.

## Applications
- On-air: screen bugs, animated bumpers, programme headers.
- Signage ("senyalistica") system documented.
- Sub-brand architecture allows modular adaptation across TV channels, radio, digital platforms.
- Toolkit ("caixa d'eines") with packaged assets referenced.

## Tone of Voice
- Defined in section 7 ("Copy / To de veu").
- Dual register: can be formal and authoritative (news, journalism) or fresh and cheerful (entertainment, culture).
- Typography choices reinforce the tonal shift (Bold caps = serious; Book mixed-case = playful).

## Outliers / Unique Elements
- Deeply culturally embedded: every design decision is justified through Valencian cultural references (paella, oranges, Mediterranean, ceramic traditions).
- The accent mark on the "A" is treated as a distinct brand element in its own right.
- Entire document written in Valencian/Catalan, reinforcing the public service mission of linguistic promotion.
- Children's sub-brand "La Colla" explicitly exempted from standard colour rules.

## Quality Score
4 / 5 -- Comprehensive brand system with strong cultural rationale, detailed logo construction, colour specifications with full Pantone/CMYK/RGB/Hex values, and a clear sub-brand architecture. Minor gaps: photography direction is thin, and tone-of-voice section is brief relative to the visual system.
